matches.rationale: Prediction 6 identifies the ambiguous budget overlap in CPT involving replay data, which is the same issue as the ground truth's unclear compounding of token budgets in Section 2.1.
Predictions 1 and 11 both highlight the flawed 1B vs 4B comparison in Table 1 and Takeaway 2 that ignores FLOPs, matching the ground truth's concern about selective presentation of results.
No finding addresses the contradiction between the claim that RL data is disjoint from SFT and evidence of overlap.
No finding identifies the overstatement of CPT's bridging role in the abstract, which the ground truth flags as claim distortion.
No finding points out that FineMath or NuminaMath are fabricated references.
No finding mentions the omission of ethical, IRB, or bias considerations in the abstract's release statement.
No finding calls out the overgeneralized conclusion about ORM scores as reliable indicators or the insufficient limitation acknowledgment.

No finding captures the inconsistency where the abstract claims full open-sourcing but later sections lack dataset details and links. Prediction 9 addresses a different proprietary-vs-open contradiction.

Prediction 3 directly flags the drastic performance drop at 350K/400K examples and questions the clarity of the explanation, matching the ground truth's concern about unreported training instabilities.
No finding discusses omitted bias, fairness, or representativeness assessment in the method descriptions.
No finding mentions missing error bars or statistical variance in Figure 1.
Prediction 8 identifies that exact ORM score computation details and normalization are missing from Appendix B.3, matching the ground truth's ambiguity about the formula.
No finding calls out the omission of OOD accuracy decreases in takeaways, which overstates the positive scaling view.
No finding addresses the missing hyperparameter and evaluation details for baseline comparisons in Table 4.
No finding discusses the limitation of studying only final checkpoints, which the ground truth identifies as an experimental design gap.
Prediction 2 exactly captures the inconsistency between Section 4.1's warning about intermediate checkpoints and Section 3's heavy reliance on them.
No finding flags the promotional tone and rhetoric in the related work section.
No finding mentions the absence of responsible disclosure guidance or risk assessment in the reproducibility appendix.
